findings.problem: ShardWorkflow has no typestate enum or state machine. Any combination of status/is_validated/is_sent is representable, including validated-but-not-sent, sent-but-status-not-"sent", or validated-and-sent simultaneously without causal ordering.
findings.failure_mode: Callers construct ShardWorkflow with invalid state combinations (e.g. is_sent=true with status="created"), violating domain invariants silently.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, is_sent with a single ShardState enum (e.g. Created, Validated, Sent) whose variants own all lifecycle data. Remove all three fields.

findings.problem: status is a pub String, allowing any arbitrary string value ("sent", "SENT", "", "delivered", typos). This makes pattern matching impossible and state logic implicit in string comparison.
findings.failure_mode: A caller sets status="SENT" (uppercase) and the system treats it as a non-sent state, or an empty string passes validation checks that only check for specific values.
findings.fix: Replace with a sealed Status enum (Created, Validated, Sent). Use match on the enum variant instead of string comparison. The enum constructor enforces the finite set of valid statuses.

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are bare pub booleans. They encode independent lifecycle flags that have causal ordering (validation must precede sending) but the type system cannot express this.
findings.failure_mode: A caller sets is_sent=true without is_validated=true, creating an unsent-then-sent state that bypasses validation. The boolean flags are independently mutable, allowing transitions backwards (sent->not-sent).
findings.fix: Fold both booleans into a single ShardState enum with ordered variants (Created -> Validated -> Sent). Remove is_validated and is_sent. mark_sent becomes a method on Validated that returns Sent.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is Option<u64> decoupled from lifecycle booleans. The timestamp can be Some even when is_sent=false, or None when is_sent=true — no invariant ties lifecycle data to the lifecycle state.
findings.failure_mode: A shard appears unsent (is_sent=false) but has a sent timestamp (Some), causing downstream consumers to double-send or mis-report. Or a sent shard has None timestamp, losing audit trail.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of the ShardState enum: enum ShardState { Created, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. Option lifetime data belongs to the variant that owns it (skill line 80).

findings.problem: id is pub String — a raw primitive that carries no domain rules. Any string, including empty, whitespace, or non-unique values, is accepted. Callers cannot distinguish Shard ids from other string IDs.
findings.failure_mode: A caller passes an empty string or duplicate id as Shard id. The domain has no way to reject invalid ids at the type level, pushing validation to runtime string checks.
findings.fix: Introduce a ShardId newtype: pub struct ShardId(String). Provide a smart constructor that validates (non-empty, trimmed) and returns Result<ShardId, Error>. Use ShardId instead of String in the struct.

findings.problem: There is no parse boundary in this module. Raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) cross module boundaries without fallible smart constructors. mark_sent accepts a fully-formed ShardWorkflow and mutates it in place, meaning callers can construct invalid domain states directly and pass them in.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct ShardWorkflow { id: "".to_string(), status: "".to_string(), is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } and pass it to mark_sent, creating an invalid but irrecoverable in-place mutation.
findings.fix: Create fallible smart constructors for each lifecycle stage: ShardWorkflow::create(id) -> Result<ShardWorkflow, Error>, Validated::from(ShardWorkflow) -> Result<Validated, Error>, Sent::from(Validated, timestamp) -> Sent. mark_sent operates on Validated and returns Sent, enforcing the transition at the type level.

findings.problem: All struct fields are pub, allowing any code to mutate status, booleans, and timestamp directly. This bypasses all domain invariants and makes the struct a public data bag rather than a domain object.
findings.failure_mode: External code sets item.is_validated = true without any validation logic, or sets item.status = "anything" directly, completely bypassing mark_sent and any validation gate.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide constructor functions (ShardWorkflow::create) and lifecycle transition methods (validate(), mark_sent()) that enforce invariants. Use the typestate enum approach so transitions are type-enforced.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership and mutates the struct in place with side-effect-like behavior (string allocation, boolean flip). It returns the same struct type, so there is no type-enforced state transition. The function name implies an action but the struct type doesn't change.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish a pre-sent from post-sent shard at compile time. The function is a pure function disguised as a state transition — no validation of preconditions (is_validated?) is performed, allowing sending unvalidated shards.
findings.fix: Split into type-enforced transitions: fn validate(item: ShardWorkflow) -> Result<Validated, Error>, fn mark_sent(v: Validated, now_ms: u64) -> Sent. Each transition validates preconditions and returns a different type.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists — no baseline, no workload, no measured performance claim to evaluate
no profiler data — no hot path identified, no allocation profiles, no cache behavior analysis
no allocation evidence — ShardWorkflow allocates on every mark_sent call (status: "sent".to_string()), no try_reserve or allocation budget
no second-ring evidence — no command output, no test output, no proof artifacts for any invariant
no command-truth evidence — mark_sent claims to be a domain action but has no I/O boundary or command tracing
no tests — the crate has zero test coverage, no behavior tests, no property tests
residual_risk: Struct uses raw String for status and lifecycle booleans — illegal states are fully representable. No typestate machine, no parse boundary, no encapsulation. Every field is pub and independently mutable. mark_sent performs no precondition checks and cannot enforce ordering. Without refactoring to an enum-based typestate with smart constructors, the domain model cannot prevent invalid shard states at compile time. This is a foundational architecture violation that blocks all downstream Holzman guarantees.
